newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Council to debate future of EU consumer policy.
newsitem.headline: Council to debate future of EU consumer policy.

text.p: The Dutch Presidency has organised an open debate at Thursday's consumer Council on the future of EU consumer policy.

The object of the debate at the Luxembourg Council meeting will be to examine how the EU's focus can move away from consumer protection to consumer policy, using consumer associations, for example, rather than market intervention.

The move responds to what the Dutch Presidency sees as an imbalance in consumer policy at the European Commission at the moment, with too much emphasis on intervention in markets, and too little on use of consumer associations, diplomats said.
Among the questions the ministers will be asked to address are how the functioning of the market can be used to strengthen the position of the consumer and what role consumer organisations can play.

They will also be asked in what cases Community intervention is needed to ensure that consumers can play as effectively as possible their role as market participants and whether areas of consumer legislation should be identified for a possible review or for further simplification.
